primaryGoal: Identify the top 3 worst performing Opportunity Source MQL Categories and their associated campaigns based on the highest drop from M0 to M1 opportunity counts for the current month.
assumptions: The [Opportunity M0 Date] and [Opportunity M1 Date] fields accurately represent the timing of opportunity creation at each stage.
A higher drop from M0 to M1 indicates worse performance, suggesting lower conversion or progression rates.
The current month refers to the most recent complete calendar month in the dataset.
The filters [Opportunity Source] = 'marketing', [Opportunity Source MQL Classification] = 'digital and events', and [Opportunity Deployment] != 'mode' are consistently applied across all data pulls.
All required data for M0 and M1 can be fetched in separate queries and then combined for drop calculation.

phases.phaseTitle: Category-Level M0 and M1 Data Collection
phases.phaseDescription: This phase focuses on fetching M0 and M1 opportunity counts separately at the Opportunity Source MQL Category level, along with campaign-level details. This comprehensive data pull will enable us to calculate drops and identify worst performers without requiring additional fetches.

fetchSteps.title: Fetch 1: M0 Opportunity Counts by Category and Campaign
fetchSteps.objective: Retrieve all M0 opportunity counts for the current month, grouped by Opportunity Source MQL Category and Campaign Name, with all required filters applied.
fetchSteps.requiredData: Columns: [Opportunity Source MQL Category], [Opportunity MQL Touch Last Campaign Name], SUM of [f Opportunity M0 Created Count]. Filters: [Opportunity Source] = 'marketing', [Opportunity Source MQL Classification] = 'digital and events', [Opportunity Deployment] != 'mode', [Opportunity M0 Date] in current month. Aggregation: SUM of [f Opportunity M0 Created Count] grouped by [Opportunity Source MQL Category] and [Opportunity MQL Touch Last Campaign Name].
fetchSteps.fetchPrompt: Fetch all opportunities where [Opportunity M0 Date] is in the current month and [Opportunity Source] equals 'marketing' and [Opportunity Source MQL Classification] equals 'digital and events' and [Opportunity Deployment] does not equal 'mode'. Include columns [Opportunity Source MQL Category], [Opportunity MQL Touch Last Campaign Name], and the sum of [f Opportunity M0 Created Count] grouped by [Opportunity Source MQL Category] and [Opportunity MQL Touch Last Campaign Name].
fetchSteps.phaseTitle: Category-Level M0 and M1 Data Collection

fetchSteps.title: Fetch 2: M1 Opportunity Counts by Category and Campaign
fetchSteps.objective: Retrieve all M1 opportunity counts for the current month, grouped by Opportunity Source MQL Category and Campaign Name, with all required filters applied.
fetchSteps.requiredData: Columns: [Opportunity Source MQL Category], [Opportunity MQL Touch Last Campaign Name], SUM of [f Opportunity M1 Created Count]. Filters: [Opportunity Source] = 'marketing', [Opportunity Source MQL Classification] = 'digital and events', [Opportunity Deployment] != 'mode', [Opportunity M1 Date] in current month. Aggregation: SUM of [f Opportunity M1 Created Count] grouped by [Opportunity Source MQL Category] and [Opportunity MQL Touch Last Campaign Name].
fetchSteps.fetchPrompt: Fetch all opportunities where [Opportunity M1 Date] is in the current month and [Opportunity Source] equals 'marketing' and [Opportunity Source MQL Classification] equals 'digital and events' and [Opportunity Deployment] does not equal 'mode'. Include columns [Opportunity Source MQL Category], [Opportunity MQL Touch Last Campaign Name], and the sum of [f Opportunity M1 Created Count] grouped by [Opportunity Source MQL Category] and [Opportunity MQL Touch Last Campaign Name].
fetchSteps.phaseTitle: Category-Level M0 and M1 Data Collection

analysisSteps.title: Analysis 1: Calculate Total M0 Count by Category
analysisSteps.aggregation: SUM of [f Opportunity M0 Created Count]
analysisSteps.question: What is the total M0 opportunity count for each Opportunity Source MQL Category in the current month?
analysisSteps.analysisPrompt: Using the fetched data, group by [Opportunity Source MQL Category] and calculate the sum of [f Opportunity M0 Created Count] for each category. Present the results as a table showing each category and its total M0 count. This will serve as the baseline for identifying categories with the highest drops.
analysisSteps.phaseTitle: Category-Level M0 and M1 Data Collection

analysisSteps.title: Analysis 2: Calculate Total M1 Count by Category
analysisSteps.aggregation: SUM of [f Opportunity M1 Created Count]
analysisSteps.question: What is the total M1 opportunity count for each Opportunity Source MQL Category in the current month?
analysisSteps.analysisPrompt: Using the fetched data, group by [Opportunity Source MQL Category] and calculate the sum of [f Opportunity M1 Created Count] for each category. Present the results as a table showing each category and its total M1 count. This will be compared against M0 counts to identify drop magnitudes.
analysisSteps.phaseTitle: Category-Level M0 and M1 Data Collection

phases.phaseTitle: Category-Level Drop Analysis and Top 3 Identification
phases.phaseDescription: This phase combines the M0 and M1 data from Phase 1 to calculate the absolute drop (M0 - M1) for each Opportunity Source MQL Category and identifies the top 3 categories with the highest drops.

fetchSteps.title: Analysis Only: Combine M0 and M1 Data for Category-Level Drop Calculation
fetchSteps.objective: Calculate the drop from M0 to M1 for each category using the aggregated results from steps 1.1.1 and 1.2.1.
fetchSteps.requiredData: Data from Analysis 1.1.1 (M0 counts by category) and Analysis 1.2.1 (M1 counts by category).
fetchSteps.fetchPrompt: No new fetch required. Use the results from Analysis 1.1.1 and Analysis 1.2.1.
fetchSteps.phaseTitle: Category-Level Drop Analysis and Top 3 Identification

analysisSteps.title: Analysis 3: Calculate M0 to M1 Drop by Category
analysisSteps.question: Which Opportunity Source MQL Categories have the highest absolute drop from M0 to M1 in the current month?
analysisSteps.analysisPrompt: Combine the results from Analysis 1.1.1 (M0 counts) and Analysis 1.2.1 (M1 counts) by matching on [Opportunity Source MQL Category]. For each category, calculate the drop as (M0 Count - M1 Count). Sort the categories by drop in descending order and identify the top 3 categories with the highest drops. Present the results as a table with columns: [Opportunity Source MQL Category], [M0 Count], [M1 Count], [Drop (M0 - M1)]. Clearly highlight the top 3 worst performing categories.
analysisSteps.phaseTitle: Category-Level Drop Analysis and Top 3 Identification

phases.phaseTitle: Campaign-Level Drop Analysis for Top 3 Categories
phases.phaseDescription: This phase drills down into the top 3 worst performing categories identified in Phase 2 to determine which specific campaigns within each category experienced the highest drops from M0 to M1.

fetchSteps.title: Analysis Only: Calculate Campaign-Level Drops for Top 3 Categories
fetchSteps.objective: For each of the top 3 worst performing categories, calculate the M0 to M1 drop at the campaign level using data from Fetch 1.1 and Fetch 1.2.
fetchSteps.requiredData: Data from Fetch 1.1 (M0 counts by category and campaign) and Fetch 1.2 (M1 counts by category and campaign), filtered to include only the top 3 categories identified in Analysis 2.1.1.
fetchSteps.fetchPrompt: No new fetch required. Use the results from Fetch 1.1 and Fetch 1.2, filtered for the top 3 categories identified in Analysis 2.1.1.
fetchSteps.phaseTitle: Campaign-Level Drop Analysis for Top 3 Categories

analysisSteps.title: Analysis 4: Identify Worst Performing Campaigns within Top 3 Categories
analysisSteps.groupBy: [Opportunity Source MQL Category], [Opportunity MQL Touch Last Campaign Name]
analysisSteps.aggregation: Calculated Metric: (M0 Count - M1 Count) at campaign level
analysisSteps.question: For each of the top 3 worst performing Opportunity Source MQL Categories, which campaigns had the highest drop from M0 to M1?
analysisSteps.analysisPrompt: Using the detailed data from Fetch 1.1 (M0 by category and campaign) and Fetch 1.2 (M1 by category and campaign), filter the data to include only the top 3 categories identified in Analysis 2.1.1. For each category, match M0 and M1 data by [Opportunity MQL Touch Last Campaign Name] and calculate the drop as (M0 Count - M1 Count) for each campaign. Within each of the top 3 categories, sort campaigns by drop in descending order and identify the campaign(s) with the highest drop. Present the results in three separate tables (one for each top category) with columns: [Opportunity Source MQL Category], [Opportunity MQL Touch Last Campaign Name], [M0 Count], [M1 Count], [Drop (M0 - M1)]. Highlight the worst performing campaign within each category and provide a summary insight explaining which campaigns are underperforming and may require immediate attention or optimization.
analysisSteps.phaseTitle: Campaign-Level Drop Analysis for Top 3 Categories

phases.phaseDescription: This final phase synthesizes all findings from the previous phases to deliver clear, actionable insights and recommendations for addressing the worst performing categories and campaigns.

fetchSteps.title: Analysis Only: Synthesize Findings and Generate Recommendations
fetchSteps.objective: Consolidate all analysis results to provide a comprehensive view of worst performers and actionable next steps.
fetchSteps.requiredData: Results from Analysis 2.1.1 (top 3 worst categories) and Analysis 3.1.1 (worst campaigns within those categories).
fetchSteps.fetchPrompt: No new fetch required. Use consolidated results from all previous analyses.

analysisSteps.title: Analysis 5: Generate Executive Summary and Recommendations
analysisSteps.question: What are the key insights about the worst performing categories and campaigns, and what actions should be taken?
analysisSteps.analysisPrompt: Create an executive summary that includes: (1) The top 3 worst performing Opportunity Source MQL Categories with their M0 to M1 drop magnitudes and percentages; (2) For each category, the specific campaign(s) with the highest drops; (3) Potential reasons for poor performance (e.g., targeting issues, creative fatigue, market saturation); (4) Actionable recommendations such as pausing underperforming campaigns, reallocating budget to better performers, conducting A/B tests, or refining audience targeting. Present this as a clear, business-focused narrative with bullet points for easy consumption by stakeholders.
